keyTerms.definition: The instructors of the CS229 foundations course.
Minimum sufficient explanation, strong answer, red flags, rubric, remediation.

recall.question: What is this file?
recall.answer: Keys for the unit U14 interview questions. Each answer gives the minimum sufficient explanation, a strong answer, common red flags, a rubric, and remediation.

keyTerms.definition: One symbol the model reads.
Repeatedly merge the most frequent adjacent pair.

recall.question: B1: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: a token is one symbol the model reads (word, piece, punctuation, byte, marker). BPE starts from bytes/characters and repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent pair.

keyTerms.definition: p(x_1, ..., x_T) = prod_t p(x_t | x_{<t}).
Support |V|^T is astronomical; each conditional has support |V|.

recall.question: B2: What is the minimum sufficient answer?

keyTerms.definition: (1/T) sum_t l_ce(f_theta(x_{<t}), x_t).
The next token; the per-position |V|-way classification reading.

recall.question: B3: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: (1/T) sum_t l_ce(f_theta(x_0, ..., x_{t-1}), x_t), averaged over sequences, AdamW on mini-batches.

keyTerms.definition: p_{t,j} = softmax(q_t k_j^T / sqrt(d_h)).
h^out_t = sum_j p_{t,j} v_j.

recall.question: B4: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: p_{t,j} = softmax(q_t k_j^T / sqrt(d_h)), h^out_t = sum_j p_{t,j} v_j.

keyTerms.definition: The q-k dot product has variance ~d_h at initialization.
Unscaled logits saturate the softmax and kill gradients.

recall.question: B5: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: the q-k dot product has variance ~d_h at initialization, unscaled logits saturate the softmax and kill gradients. Scaling keeps logit variance near 1.

keyTerms.definition: M_{t,j} = 0 for j <= t, -infinity for j > t, before softmax.
Position t depends only on current and past tokens.

recall.question: B6: What is the minimum sufficient answer?
recall.answer: Minimum: M_{t,j} = 0 for j <= t, -infinity for j > t, added before the softmax. Guarantees the autoregressive property.

keyTerms.definition: The causal mask is absent or applied after softmax.

recall.question: What are the D1 answers?
recall.answer: D1.2: rows [1, 0, 0], [0.3302, 0.6698, 0], [0.4011, 0.4011, 0.1978]. D1.3: stacking the per-position rules gives the matrix form.

keyTerms.definition: Prefill O(T^2 d_h); decode KV cache O(T d_h) per head.
MHA 128.0 MiB, GQA 32.0 MiB, MQA 4.0 MiB per layer at T = 8192.

recall.question: What are the D2 answers?
recall.answer: D2.2: per layer at T = 8192 fp16: MHA 128.0 MiB, GQA (n_g = 8) 32.0 MiB, MQA 4.0 MiB. D2.3: the cache stores one K/V head per group.

keyTerms.definition: Row t of Q K^T / c with the causal mask.
Exactly 0 for j > t: the vector of (17.23).

recall.question: Q1: What is the answer?
recall.answer: Row t of Q K^T / c holds q_t k_j^T / c. The causal mask sets j > t to -infinity; softmax_row gives exactly 0 for j > t: the vector of (17.23).

keyTerms.definition: tau = 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 sweeps.
Append k_new/v_new before computing scores.
One query vs n_h query heads under GQA.

recall.question: T1: What is the answer?
recall.answer: Bug 1: the new key/value are appended after the attention computation, so each token never attends to its own position. Bug 2: the code assumes one key head; under GQA the query has n_h heads.

keyTerms.definition: GQA/MQA or sliding window; sacrifices long-range quality.
Cache accounting with eviction; sacrifices latency guarantees.

recall.question: S1: What is the answer?
recall.answer: Architectural: switch MHA to GQA/MQA or add sliding-window attention. Systems: per-sequence cache accounting with eviction/offload. Measure quality at 128k before shipping.

keyTerms.definition: Loss falls while answer quality does not improve.
Flip the loss mask: 1 on answers, 0 on prompts.

recall.question: S2: What is the answer?
recall.answer: Symptoms: the loss mainly predicts prompt tokens, so it falls while answer quality does not improve. Fix: flip the loss mask (1 on answer positions, 0 on prompt positions).

keyTerms.definition: Zero-shot scores depend on exact prompt wording.
Same prompts for both models; mean and spread across variants.

recall.question: R1: What is the answer?
recall.answer: Confound: zero-shot scores depend on the exact prompt wording. Protocol: fix a prompt set before seeing results, evaluate both models on the same prompts, report mean and spread.
